Get started with dazcache

Source: vignettes/dazcache.Rmd
dazcache.Rmd
library(dazcache)

We will build a small cache of market prices: store quotes under keys, find them again, let them expire, drop a group of them at once, and memoise the slow function that fetches them. By the end you will know the handful of functions most code needs. Running a cache across many processes, and how it is stored, are left to the articles listed at the end.

Open a cache

A cache is a directory. cache() opens it, creating it if needed, and every R process on the machine that opens the same directory sees the same entries. Its handle, s here, is what every other function takes first.

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "prices")
s <- cache(dir)

Store and read values

cache_set() stores a value under a key and returns the cache, so writes chain. cache_get() reads a value back.

s |>
  cache_set("XSWX/2026-08-28", c(100.8, 101.4)) |>
  cache_set("XSWX/2026-08-29", c(101.2, 101.9))

cache_get(s, "XSWX/2026-08-29")
#> [1] 101.2 101.9

Asking for a key that has no entry is the mistake you will make first. It is an error, so a missing value never passes for a real one:

cache_get(s, "XNYS/2026-08-29")
#> Error in `cache_get()`:
#> ! No entry for key "XNYS/2026-08-29".
#> ℹ Supply `default` to return a value instead of erroring.

Supply default when a miss is expected, or ask with cache_has() first. A stored NULL is a value like any other, so the two never get confused.

cache_get(s, "XNYS/2026-08-29", default = NULL)
#> NULL
cache_has(s, c("XSWX/2026-08-29", "XNYS/2026-08-29"))
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE

Choose keys

A string is its own key, and a "group/item" convention gives you prefixes to list by:

cache_keys(s, prefix = "XSWX/")
#> [1] "XSWX/2026-08-28" "XSWX/2026-08-29"

A key can also be a number, a date or a named list. The same values always find the same entry, whatever order the fields are written in:

cache_set(s, list(exchange = "XNYS", date = as.Date("2026-08-29")), c(57.8, 58.1))
cache_get(s, list(date = as.Date("2026-08-29"), exchange = "XNYS"))
#> [1] 57.8 58.1

Expire and drop entries

An entry can expire: after a number of seconds, a difftime, or at a POSIXct time. An expired entry is gone for every reader at once. Here, an intraday quote is good for an hour, and one with expire = 0 is gone as soon as it is written:

cache_set(s, "XSWX/live", 101.6, expire = as.difftime(1, units = "hours"))
cache_set(s, "XSWX/stale", 101.5, expire = 0)
cache_has(s, c("XSWX/live", "XSWX/stale"))
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE

Tags group entries for invalidation. Tag the quotes that came from one feed, and drop them all when that feed turns out to be wrong:

cache_set(s, "XLON/2026-08-28", 7.41, tags = "feed-b")
cache_set(s, "XLON/2026-08-29", 7.44, tags = "feed-b")
cache_evict(s, tag = "feed-b")
cache_keys(s, prefix = "XLON/")
#> character(0)

Memoise a function

Most quotes come from somewhere slow. cache_memoise() wraps a function so that each call is looked up first and computed only on a miss. The results outlive the session, and every process using the cache shares them. The second call below reads the first call’s result:

fetch_quotes <- function(exchange, date) {
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  set.seed(as.integer(date))
  round(runif(2, 50, 150), 1)
}
quotes <- cache_memoise(fetch_quotes, s)

system.time(quotes("XTKS", as.Date("2026-08-29")))
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   0.002   0.000   0.504
system.time(quotes("XTKS", as.Date("2026-08-29")))
#>    user  system elapsed 
#>   0.001   0.000   0.001

A call is keyed on the function’s name, here fetch_quotes, the name it was passed as, and on its arguments. The key does not depend on the function’s code: when the function changes meaning, give it a new version, and its calls get new keys.

cache_memoise_key(quotes, "XTKS", as.Date("2026-08-29"))
#> [1] "fetch_quotes/v1/{date=d:2026-08-29,exchange=s:XTKS}"
quotes <- cache_memoise(fetch_quotes, s, version = 2)
cache_memoise_key(quotes, "XTKS", as.Date("2026-08-29"))
#> [1] "fetch_quotes/v2/{date=d:2026-08-29,exchange=s:XTKS}"

Large values and the catalogue

A year of ticks is too large to keep inside the database. A value of 32 KiB or more (inline_max) is stored as a read-only RDS file, and cache_path() gives that file to tools that read it in place:

ticks <- runif(1e5, 100, 102)
cache_set(s, "XSWX/2026/ticks", ticks)
path <- cache_path(s, "XSWX/2026/ticks")
identical(readRDS(path), ticks)
#> [1] TRUE

cache_entries() lists what the cache holds as a data frame: each key, its size in bytes as stored, whether it lives inside the database, and when it expires. A key that is not a string is listed by its text form, which How a cache stores keys and values explains.

cache_entries(s)[, c("key", "bytes", "inline", "expires")]
#>                                                   key  bytes inline
#> 1                                     XSWX/2026-08-28     47   TRUE
#> 2                                     XSWX/2026-08-29     47   TRUE
#> 3                                     XSWX/2026/ticks 800031  FALSE
#> 4                                           XSWX/live     39   TRUE
#> 5 fetch_quotes/v1/{date=d:2026-08-29,exchange=s:XTKS}     47   TRUE
#> 6                 {date=d:2026-08-29,exchange=s:XNYS}     47   TRUE
#>               expires
#> 1                <NA>
#> 2                <NA>
#> 3                <NA>
#> 4 2026-11-16 17:02:54
#> 5                <NA>
#> 6                <NA>

When you are done, close the cache. Its entries stay on disk for the next process.

cache_close(s)
